finding: A probe's own test execution is indistinguishable from a clean baseline in `runs.ndjson`, so the next probe can adopt it as its baseline. §5.2.4 says "Every run MUST be stored as a **run record** in `runs.ndjson`" and lists its fields — `id`, `head`, `filter`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `tests_run`, `tests_failed`, `output_tail`, `passed` — none of which records that the run was performed under a mutation or a probe test file. §5.5's `baseline` row demands a run "measuring the same tests on unmutated, un-probed code", but §5.2.6 resolves it mechanically: "`cr probe run` MUST resolve its baseline per §5.5 and, when no matching run exists at the current head, MUST perform and record it before the probe. When more than one matches, the most recent MUST be used." The only match criteria available are head and filter, and the most recent match at a given (head, filter) after one mutation probe has run is that probe's own mutated run. When the first probe returned `no-test-failed` — exit 0, `tests_run` > 0, `tests_failed` 0 — that run is `passed: true` under §5.2.5, so a second mutation probe with the same filter satisfies §5.3.5's guard ("only when the probe's `baseline` run record has `passed: true`") against a measurement taken on mutated code, which is precisely what the baseline exists to exclude, and the finding reaches `probed` and is posted as an assertion. Two mutation probes sharing a filter at one head is the ordinary workflow, not a corner case. The only alternative reading — that probe runs are not written to `runs.ndjson` — contradicts §5.2.4's "Every run".
suggestion: In §5.2.4 add `probe` to the run record's field list, carrying the probe id when the run was performed as part of a probe, and in §5.2.6 add: "Only a run record carrying no `probe` may serve as a baseline."

finding: `target` is `computed for `mutation`` and required on every probe record (§5.5), but §5.3.2 defines its derivation only as "`cr` MUST derive `target` from the patch itself — the first line the diff modifies", and never says which coordinate space the line number is read in or what happens when the patch modifies no existing line. A unified-diff hunk header carries both an old-file range and a new-file range. §5.5 says the target is "always `side: RIGHT` since probes run against the sandbox at head", and §6.2.2 checks it against `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line`, which are head coordinates — so the value must be the pre-image (sandbox-at-head) line number, not the post-image number the applied patch produces. Nothing states that, and the two coincide only for pure replacements. Worse, the canonical mutation is an insertion — dropping an early `return` into a function — whose hunk has no `-` line at all, so "the first line the diff modifies" selects nothing and I cannot produce the required field. I would have to invent both the coordinate space and the insertion-only fallback, and getting either wrong silently breaks the §6.2.2 containment guard that is the sole barrier against one experiment grading a different finding.
suggestion: In §5.3.2 replace "the first line the diff modifies" with: "the pre-image line number of the first line the patch removes or replaces; for a hunk that only adds lines, the pre-image line the additions are inserted after, or the hunk's first pre-image line when it inserts at the top."

finding: §4.4.3 says "A test-adequacy finding asserts only with an experiment. Citations to test files MUST NOT grade it `cited`, so without a supporting probe it is `argued` and is posted as a question per §6.3." But §6.2 — the section that actually computes the grade — carries no such branch. Its table grades `cited` on "at least one entry in `citations` that `cr` resolved against the current head, and that entry either has `origin: rule` or lies outside the record's own unit", and §6.2.1 closes the input set: "The only inputs are `citations` and the referenced probe record". A test file almost always lies outside the reviewed unit's hunks, so an implementer following §6.2 grades a test-adequacy record `cited`, §6.3.1's forcing never fires, and the record is posted as an assertion that the code is untested on the strength of a citation that establishes nothing about coverage. The obligation exists only in the axis section and is unreachable from the grading engine. §4.4.3's second sentence is also narrower than its first: a test-adequacy record citing a production file outside its own unit reaches `cited` even under §4.4.3's own text, so the axis buys the assertion register without an experiment.
suggestion: End §6.2's `cited` row with ", and the record's `axis` is not `test`", and add `axis` to §6.2.1's enumerated inputs.

finding: §7.1.5 says "`cr` MUST write each record's agent region exactly as rendered to `rounds/<n>/rendered.json`" and §7.1.6 says regeneration "MUST then preserve bodies for records whose body differs from `rendered.json`". Neither says what `rendered.json` holds for a record whose body was *preserved* rather than re-rendered, and the two readings differ destructively. Read literally — rendered.json records what `cr` wrote into `draft.md`, and a preserved body is what it wrote — the second `cr draft` stores the edited body, so the third `cr draft` finds body == rendered.json, concludes the body is untouched, and regenerates it from `summary` and `evidence` per §8.1.2, in English. That silently destroys the only input path the spec gives for reader-facing prose (§8.1.2: "Editing the draft is the only input path"), and the round-9 deletion of the concatenated agent-region hash removed the one other mechanical trace an implementer could have used to reconstruct the intent. The other reading — rendered.json only ever holds `cr`-generated text — keeps the edit forever. I cannot pick one from the text, and one of them posts machine English to the author after the human approved a rewritten body.
suggestion: Append to §7.1.5: "`rendered.json` MUST hold only the body `cr` itself generated; a body preserved per §7.1.6 MUST NOT replace its `rendered.json` entry."

finding: §4.5.4 now names four lenses that must be disclosed — "a disabled axis, an unavailable axis, the unavailable reinvention half of §4.3.1, and a role skipped per §4.6.4" — but the only author-facing mirror was not widened with it. §8.4.3 still glosses the obligation as "the disclosure of §4.5.4 — the active axes, and the disabled and unavailable ones with their reasons — so the honesty obligation reaches the author and not only the reviewer's terminal." An implementer builds the review body from that enumeration, so a skipped role and an unavailable reinvention half never reach the author at all. This is not merely an omission: §4.5.1 defines role activity from axis activity and not the reverse, so an axis every one of whose roles was skipped per §4.6.4 is still "active", and the author reads an axis listed as active that no lens ever examined — the exact false coverage claim §4.5.4 justifies itself by ("silence about it would let a complete verdict cover a lens that never looked"). §10.1.3 repeats the narrowing in the reviewer-facing report — "Active axes, disabled and unavailable axes with reasons, and skipped roles with reasons per §4.5.4" omits the reinvention half — while §10.2's closing paragraph got the general phrasing right ("every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run").
suggestion: In §8.4.3 replace the em-dash gloss with "every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason", and make §10.1.3 read the same.

finding: §2.6 is the one section carrying both a numbered list and subsections, so `§2.6.<n>` denotes two different clauses, and the spec uses it in both senses. §2.4's `rules` row says "the third layer of §2.6.1", meaning §2.6's numbered item 1 ("Rules MUST resolve in layers, highest first: per-repository (§2.2), then global (§2.2), then the resolved profile's `rules` array") — but §2.6.1 is the heading "Detection", which says nothing about layers. §2.6.1.3 says "The rule id is carried separately on the record per §2.6.3", meaning §2.6's item 3 ("Every record produced by a rule MUST carry the rule id") — but §2.6.3 is the heading "Harvesting", which says nothing about record fields. Both references resolve, so `speccheck.py` passes them, and both send a reader to a clause that does not contain the obligation being cited. Meanwhile §2.2's `rule-stats.ndjson` row and §2.4's `detect` row use `§2.6.1` in the opposite, heading sense, and §8.1.6's "per §2.6.4" uses the list sense for a number that has no heading — three readings of one notation inside one section.
suggestion: Disambiguate the two mis-resolving references without renumbering: in §2.4's `rules` row write "the third layer of the resolution order in §2.6", and in §2.6.1.3 write "...is carried separately on the record per the rule-id requirement in §2.6". Apply the same form to §8.1.6's "§2.6.4".

finding: §4.5.5 requires every cell on the `test` axis to carry "`coverage` with `test_paths` when the role is on the `test` axis per §4.4.1", and §4.4.1 says the agent "MUST then classify the unit as covered, partially covered, or uncovered, and the classification MUST be recorded in the coverage cell together with the test paths it rested on". `cr cells record` has to validate this field (§4.5.6 already rejects an unknown unit id or an inactive role), but neither the shape nor the domain is given: whether `coverage` is a scalar classification sitting beside a sibling `test_paths`, or an object containing it; and what the three classification tokens are on the wire. Every other closed set in the spec is written as backticked literals — `pass`, `finding`, `question`, `na` two clauses earlier in this same item — while "partially covered" appears only as English prose, so I would have to invent `partially-covered`, `partial`, or `partially_covered` and the agent would have to guess the same way.
suggestion: In §4.5.5 replace "`coverage` with `test_paths`" with "`coverage` as an object carrying `classification`, one of `covered`, `partial`, or `uncovered`, and `test_paths`".

finding: The new override erases the one value that two later clauses key their obligations on, and nothing preserves it. §5.1.7 now says "A probe whose check fails MUST be recorded with result `error`, overriding the ladder outcome". §5.3.7 says "A result of `failed` disproves the gap; `cr` MUST record it and the agent MUST NOT raise the finding." and §5.4.5 caps severity for a gap probe on "A `passed` gap probe". Take a mutation probe whose ladder rung 7 yields `failed` (the suite did catch the mutation, so the gap is disproved) and whose post-run cleanliness check then fails. Implementation A records `failed` per §5.3.7 and refuses the finding; implementation B records `error` per §5.1.7's explicit precedence, and because the record now says `error` the §5.3.7 suppression cannot fire — the agent is free to raise the very test-gap question the experiment disproved, as an `argued` question. Both read the spec correctly and disagree on the recorded result and on whether the finding may be raised, and I can write the assertion for neither. The same shape hits §5.4.5: a gap probe whose ladder said `passed` and whose check failed is recorded `error`, so the "at most `medium`" bound no longer applies and severity is unbounded. The override is also indistinguishable in the record from ladder rung 3's own `error`, so no test can tell a dirty sandbox from a runner that would not start.
suggestion: Append one sentence to §5.1.7: "The ladder outcome MUST still be recorded on the probe record as `ladder_result`, and §5.3.7's suppression and §5.4.5's severity bound key on it rather than on the overriding `error`." Add the `ladder_result` row to the §5.5 table with the same per-kind vocabulary.

finding: §5.2.3 mandates a value the run record cannot hold: "A run exceeding `tests.timeout_seconds` MUST be killed and recorded as `timeout`." The run record of §5.2.4 has no `result` field and no other field that can carry `timeout` — only `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, the two counts, `output_tail`, and `passed`. The word `timeout` is a member of the probe-record vocabulary, and §5.5 states that vocabulary is per kind and "MUST NOT be shared", so §5.2.3 cannot be satisfied by borrowing it. An implementer of §5.2 has to invent a field, which is exactly the divergence the schema list exists to prevent, and a killed run then becomes indistinguishable from a runner that exited non-zero on its own.
suggestion: Add `timed_out` to §5.2.4's field list and change §5.2.3 to "...MUST be killed and recorded with `timed_out: true`."

finding: Deleting the old §4.4.2 (the agent enumerates expected edge cases per claim, bounded by `test.max_edge_cases`) left the surviving §4.4.2 with no producer and no observable effect. It now reads in full: "A missing edge case SHOULD be escalated to a probe per §5." Nothing in the spec defines, records, or bounds a "missing edge case" any more — the only other occurrence is §5.4.1's "The agent supplies a new test file targeting the suspected edge case", which is an agent input, not a set `cr` can enumerate. There is no `cr` command, no state file in §2.2 or §2.3, and no validation the clause can be asserted against: an implementation that escalates nothing and an implementation that escalates every uncovered unit are both conforming and indistinguishable to any test I can write. The clause's real content — that a test-adequacy concern needs an experiment before it may assert — is already carried in full by §4.4.3.
suggestion: Delete §4.4.2 and renumber the current §4.4.3 to §4.4.2.
